paragraphs: A browser-based marching band drill designer built with Babylon.js. Create and edit robot formations and paths on a football field, then preview synchronized movement in a 3D stadium. The scene supports desktop browsers and immersive VR or AR on compatible headsets such as Meta Quest 3.
features: Settings -> Drill form editor exposes line, arc, circle, block, polygon, and star tools for standing formations. Choose an empty origin and target spacing to add forms without replacing an imported show. Select a form…

Optional field-grid snap uses 0.3125, 0.625, 1.25, 2.5, or 5-yard intervals; angle snap uses 45 degrees. Settings and the XR palm form library share snap/spacing settings. The palm library also provides spacing,…
Show adjustable grid on field displays a separate, non-snapping turf overlay. Set its spacing from 0.5 to 20 yards; it is independent of the editor's snapping intervals.

Each block row is a separate selectable form. The original form controls edit one standing form at a time; the selection editor supports arbitrary multi-selection. Neither editor adds form saving/export or transform…

OpenMarch-style alignment tools in the same editor align X or Z to the form's average coordinate, distribute marchers evenly between the existing axis extremes, or round positions to whole yards (keyboard 1 outside text…

whatItDoes.text: A browser-based marching band drill designer built with Babylon.js. Create and edit robot formations and paths on a football field, then preview synchronized movement in a 3D stadium. The scene supports desktop browsers and immersive VR or AR on compatible headsets such as Meta Quest 3.
